style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast resting on a weathered concrete surface. On the left, a modular cloud subscription billing meter with an interlocking bay. On the right, a physical enterprise server memory bank with dense memory stick modules. Distinct physical arrangement, hard clean edges, contact shadows, one directional key light raking across them. Matte muted palette with subtle tech accents, no plain spheres, no text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, UI, watermarks, embossed text, printed lettering
rationale: A matte clay 3D render allows us to structurally contrast the two escalating cost models—a cloud meter module versus a hardware memory bank—using a clear split-screen diptych without relying on literal stock photos.

core_conflict: Predictable software subscription meters vs volatile hardware memory capital costs
